findings.text: correctness lens, critical: `_cycle_state_write_iter_atomic` is called at the END of each iteration (line 2753), so `current_iter=N` means iteration N has fully completed; when a run is interrupted mid-iter-K before that write, `current_iter=K-1` is in state, and `_start_iter=K-1` re-runs the already-completed iteration instead of the interrupted one — the formula must be `_persisted_iter + 1`. (core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh:2336; fix: code)

correctness lens, high: `zb_engine_loop_state ... 2 5 "in_progress"` runs the state writer twice (n=1 and n=2), leaving `current_iter=2` — both iterations have been recorded as completed; the comment that this represents "iter 1 completed, interrupted before iter 2 dispatched" is wrong (that scenario would leave `current_iter=1`), so the test never exercises the actual interrupted case and passes even with the off-by-one formula. (tests/integration/resume-loop-state-test.sh:51; fix: test)

correctness lens, medium: The `cycle:*` resume skip guard calls `continue` without verifying that the cycle's member artifacts are present after rehydration; unlike the `stage:*` arm which checks `! -s` on the primary artifact path and exits 1 when absent, a complete cycle whose member artifacts are missing is silently skipped, violating the RHYD-2 fail-closed requirement for cycle units. (core/pipeline/runner.sh:3446; fix: code)
